title: The Resolve to Never Look Back
text: “Naofumi-kun shows his affection in a rather clumsy way, though?”
“The Father I know has one who wears a smile just like Ark’s, I say. And more than anything, even the Father of this world overlaps with Ark, indeed.”
The moment I said it aloud, it drew even closer to certainty. I could tell that the prophetic inscription was telling me to drive this point home.
“I… once redid things in a parallel world, using the power of the spear. At that time… I witnessed all manner of different sides to Father, indeed.”
Right about then, Hou-kun came gliding back—apparently having finished his talk with Filo-tan—and caught the tail end of both my voice and Ark’s.
“Ark, I want you to tell me, I say.”

It seemed like ever since Ark and Hou-kun arrived, all I’d been doing was asking questions. But this time, even if I got scolded rather than answered kindly, I still wanted to know. That particular Father… had vanished because the conditions for looping in that parallel world had been fulfilled. Which was to say, he was none other than a Father I had failed to save. Regret naturally tightened my fists, and tears welled in my eyes. But I couldn’t afford to cry, I say. Father himself had once told me—

『It was, in the end, just something like a dream to you, Motoyasu-kun—a place different even from the afterlife. We were, so to speak, characters within a dream… there’s no real sense of death or anything like that for us.』

Characters within a dream. Death is indeed a form of parting, but from what Hou-kun and the others said, the concept of reincarnation existed. Perhaps, without even knowing it, I might meet him again in some next life. But characters within a dream didn’t even have death to begin with. Once I was certain of that, that troubled expression started to remind me of the face Father made whenever he sighed at Lazy Pig’s laziness.
“You saw yourself in me, and you want to meet him again, don’t you?”
“That’s… if I could see him again, I would want to, indeed. This time, I want to save that world’s Father for certain. That world that was erased as if it never happened… once more!”
At my answer, Ark nodded.
“…Motoyasu-kun.”
“What is it?”
“Do you have the resolve—the determination to never look back… no matter how many partings you face, can you go on without regret?”
Was that the same question he’d asked Filo-tan?
“I will never, ever part from Father or Filo-tan, I say! This Motoyasu shall remain loyal no matter what comes, indeed! I’ll pile up regrets by the thousands if I must, I say!”
“Wow, talk about doubling down—asked if you’ll regret it and you answer you’ll just stack up regrets endlessly! Amazing! Truly one of the focal points of that world.”
“Haha… with that resolve and that answer, I suppose that’ll do?”
“I see… your resolve does seem firm. I can tell you’re not all talk.”
“I see, I see, hahaha. Well now, this is turning out to be quite interesting. I’d had a faint sense of the possibility, but I never imagined it would actually come to this.”
At that, Hou-kun burst into loud, teasing laughter. Just what exactly was so amusing about all this, I wondered.
“Starting with Ren-kun, then Sadeena-san, and now even Motoyasu-kun getting right to the heart of it.”
“Ren and Older Sister, you mean?”
Had I been beaten to it, then?
“No, it was a different question than the one I asked Ren-kun or Sadeena-san. Though the cat here does have her fair share of openings, so to speak.”
“I’d rather you didn’t go around saying I have ‘openings’ without asking. Hah…”
Ark let out a deep sigh.
“Hey. Bird, did you manage to talk with Filo-chan?”
“Oh, sure. Look, she’s right over there.”

When I turned around, there was Filo-tan, hiding as if holding back out of consideration for me, tucked away behind the bushes. Ark smiled and beckoned to her, but Filo-tan just looked at me and blushed.
“Well… I suppose that’s fine. Might be good to ask a favor of both Filo-chan and Motoyasu-kun.”
“What is it, I say?”
“You… even the Naofumi-kun and the others you parted from, in order to return to this world—they matter to you too, don’t they?”
“Of course they do, indeed! Even if it’s a world people say never existed, I remember Father being there, I say!”
At my reply, Ark smiled.
“Doesn’t exist, yet exists… huh.”
“Fufu… that must be a welcome way of putting it, coming from you, wouldn’t it?”
“That’s right. Exists yet doesn’t, doesn’t exist yet does.”
Ark placed a hand on my spear. Then, all at once—several great Filolial-sama wings, the very ones that had vanished when I returned to this world, appeared once more!
“Bird, lend a hand too, would you?”
“Sure, sure. Change of plans, huh.”
“Hmm… with Filo-chan, this method would be difficult, so… let’s use that other approach instead.”
“The method of binding causality, you mean. That would give Naofumi-kun and the others more cards to play with, huh.”
Ark and Hou-kun seemed to be conferring about something, after which Hou-kun beckoned Filo-tan over. Reluctantly, Filo-tan approached.
“Now hold still, okay~?”
“Uuu…”
“Motoyasu-kun, we’ll handle things on our end, so Filo-chan, you just stay put there.”
Something like faintly glowing threads gently drifted forth and began wrapping around Filo-tan.
“Wh-what, what is this?!”
“Don’t worry, it’s nothing strange like that. Now then, Filo-chan. Your distant, distant ancestor was once a vassal of mine, so to speak—and now, I’m formally appointing you as my vassal.”
The great Filolial wings, the feather Hou-kun himself had plucked, and Filo-tan’s own feathers all turned to light and showered down upon her.
“Well, if you ever want to quit, you can quit anytime—but if you do, you’ll have to give up following Naofumi-kun, understand.”
“Uuu… Filo’s not giving up!”
“There you go, keep it up~”
“That’s a rather half-hearted way to cheer someone on, don’t you think… Well, in any case, spirits, if you would lend us your strength.”

It wasn’t Ark but Hou-kun who called out—and at that, the spear in my hands began to glow, and as if in perfect timing, a staff appeared from seemingly nowhere. This… could this be the so-called Sacred Weapon of the staff that the reincarnator once wielded?
“Good, good. The Sacred Weapon of the spear is lending its cooperation too.”
“Ah, so you’re willing to cooperate as well. I wonder if it’s compatible? Cat?”
“Sure, sure.”

With that, Ark took hold of the staff, removed its tip… and fitted a spearhead in its place. What remained could only be described as a spear. The former staff, now transformed into a spear, floated there for a moment before its gem overlapped with the one on my own spear. Something crackled and surged through, and the transformed staff vanished from sight.
“Looks like the conversion went well.”
“Yeah. Best make sure Naofumi-kun and the others don’t notice, though.”
Ark and the others seemed to be up to something.
“Well, we originally had various plans in motion, but since we’ve heard Motoyasu-kun and the others’ resolve, there’s been a change of plans.”
“What is it you intend to do, I say?”
“Right… actually, there’s something more I’d like to ask Motoyasu-kun.”
“What is it?”
“You know… after you live out a peaceful life in this world and your time comes to an end—after you die—what do you want to happen to you then?”
“What do you mean by that, I say? Wouldn’t I simply go somewhere ordinary, like heaven or hell?”
Wasn’t that how it worked—once you died, your soul went on to the afterlife or some such place? Since Hou-kun had mentioned purgatory earlier, I supposed hell existed too, then.

“I don’t know what happens after death, but of course, I intend to die in a proper, natural way… and if there truly is such a thing as reincarnation, then surely all my memories will be lost. If possible, I’d like to meet Filolial-sama again even in my next life, indeed.”
“I see… then, I suppose I’d better tell you.”
What was that supposed to mean? That didn’t sound like the answer I’d imagined at all. A bad feeling crept over me.

“It’s just… I feel rather sorry for you, I suppose. Once your lifespan comes to an end, you’ll end up back in your original world, Japan, running on that spinning wheel of parallel branching all over again… I suppose it’s simply the law of your world, but that sounds rather rough, doesn’t it.”
“Well, the laws of the world differ from place to place, after all. As for the spirit of the spear, I suppose it saved you from death even as it pulled you out of it, but…”

“Reading the mastermind’s methods, it seems like the other candidates were killed off so the first choice couldn’t be summoned. A method that exploits the spirit’s nature—its inability to overlook a death right in front of it, hoping it will act.”
“What exactly do you mean by that, I say?”
Ark and the others seemed to be saying something rather ominous. Wasn’t this supposed to be about Father?
